items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: his son is playing lead guitar for Rod Stewart in Europe for a year

ctx.x: Change the music a little bit.

Yeah. I’ve got an old-time guitar player friend who called me up not long ago, and his son is playing lead guitar for Rod Stewart in Europe for a year, and he makes, this guy I suppose in his career if he made three or four hundred dollars a week it was a good week. His son makes five thousand dollars a week, plus a hundred and forty dollars a day for food you know and stuff, and he told me, he described the column speakers they had and everything. And he said that the over-thirty guys who go to listen to this…

I know. I think the sound people have to justify themselves, so they’ve got to push things you know. And even here sometimes, I sometimes feel like, I mean sometimes things have to be amplified, if you’re playing a huge place. But sometimes I wonder, couldn’t you hang a big mic over the band and pick up the band?
